summary:
Space Relics: Every Object Has a Story is an interactive project that helps young people learn about NASA's retired and inactive spacecraft and equipment.

Our project focuses on equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Instead of seeing these objects as old or forgotten machines, users can discover their stories and learn about the important science and missions connected to them.

Users can explore an interactive map, learn about different space objects, listen to their stories, and complete fun science quests and mini-games. The project is designed for school-age students and teachers to make space history and science easier and more interesting to understand.

Our goal is to show that these objects are not just discarded machines. They are part of human history and can inspire the next generation to explore space.
details:
Space Relics is an interactive digital experience that helps young people learn about NASA's retired and inactive spacecraft and equipment. Our project focuses on objects left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.

Users can explore an interactive map and choose different objects to learn about. Each object has its own story, including what it was built for, what it discovered, and why it is still important today. Users can also take part in science quests and mini-games to make learning more fun and interactive.

Our project is creative because it turns space equipment into characters that can tell their own stories. This makes space history easier and more interesting for young people to understand.

We designed Space Relics for school-age students and teachers. We also considered accessibility by including ideas such as audio narration, captions, simple language, and multilingual content.

The main goal of our project is to show that NASA's discarded equipment is not just old machinery. These objects are part of human history and can still inspire future generations to learn about science and space exploration.
